abstract: Additive-mediated enhancement of self-assembled monolayers (SAMs) properties is essential for the synergistic regulation of perovskite crystallization and interfacial charge transport. Here, we incorporated 2,2′-biimidazole (BI) into SAMs (MeO-2PACz, [2-(3,6-dimethoxy-9H-carbazol-9-yl)ethyl]phosphonic acid) precursors, enhancing not only the adsorption behavior of SAMs but also improving the quality of the perovskite. Theoretical and experimental results indicate strong π–π interactions between BI and the carbazole units in MeO-2PACz, thereby enhancing the uniformity of the SAMs. Simultaneously, the N presenting Lewis base in BI can bind to the uncoordinated Pb2+ at the perovskite terminals, forming stable bidentate coordination. Additionally, the introduction of BI significantly optimizes the arrangement of interface energy levels and reduces residual stress in perovskite, which facilitates charge transport at the interface and enhances the intrinsic stability of the perovskite film. Consequently, the developed device achieved a maximum power conversion efficiency of 25.59%, while the wide-bandgap (1.68 eV) inverted perovskite solar cell delivered an efficiency of 23.03%.

summary.how: Additive incorporation into SAM precursors, with theoretical and experimental characterization and device fabrication.
summary.impact: Low relevance. Experimental perovskite solar cell work with no phonon or thermal content.
summary.what: Adds 2,2'-biimidazole to MeO-2PACz self-assembled monolayers to improve perovskite quality and interfacial charge transport, reaching 25.59% efficiency, and 23.03% for a 1.68 eV wide-bandgap inverted cell.
summary.why: Additive-mediated SAM enhancement regulates perovskite crystallization and interface charge transport.

title: Engineering buried termination by molecular bridge induced efficient inverted perovskite solar cells

abstract: Abstract Markov state models (MSMs) are widely used to extract kinetic information from atomistic simulations, yet they remain largely opaque, requiring complex post hoc analysis to relate macroscopic states to underlying physical interactions. This disconnect severely limits the interpretability of the automated kinetic state decomposition. Here we introduce the Kinetic Interaction Tree (KinTree), an interpretable, interaction-centric machine learning framework for kinetic modeling. KinTree represents conformational dynamics in a feature space defined by noncovalent interactions and employs a decision-tree architecture optimized by a unified kinetic-structural objective function. This design enables the direct identification of kinetically relevant interactions while producing Markovian state decompositions from raw trajectory data. KinTree is validated across diverse molecular systems, demonstrating kinetic consistency through the Chapman–Kolmogorov tests and its ability to resolve mechanistic pathways. KinTree captures complex, concurrent inter- and intrachain interactions and sensitively identifies mutation-induced rewiring of interaction networks. By integrating kinetic modeling with physically interpretable features, KinTree provides a more highly interpretable and versatile approach for molecular interactions than existing kinetic models.

summary.how: Decision-tree architecture on interaction features, validated by Chapman–Kolmogorov tests across several molecular systems.
summary.impact: Low-to-moderate relevance. A biomolecular application, but the interpretable, feature-based analysis of MD trajectories is conceptually related to MLIP interpretability and latent-space analysis.
summary.what: Introduces KinTree, an interpretable decision-tree framework for kinetic modeling of atomistic simulations. It uses noncovalent-interaction features and a unified kinetic-structural objective to produce Markovian state decompositions from raw trajectories.
summary.why: Markov state models are opaque and need post hoc analysis to link states to physical interactions.

title: Rule-Based Machine Learning for Interpretable Kinetic Modeling

abstract: Abstract Conventional near-infrared (NIR) light sensing materials, reliant on inorganic or organic semiconductors, are often limited by their photoelectric conversion efficiency, cooling volume, and recyclability. Inspired by the pit organ of rattlesnakes, this work presents an NIR sensing strategy based on photo-thermal-electric conversion. An NIR sensing unit is constructed based on Au@ITO-graphite asymmetric electrodes and ionogel, effectively coupling interfacial photothermal and thermoelectric conversion. NIR light energy is rapidly converted into heat due to the localized surface plasmon resonance (LSPR) of Au nanoparticles (Au NPs). This thermal stimulus induces asynchronous ion adsorption and desorption at asymmetric electrode–electrolyte interfaces, generating a measurable open-circuit voltage even under nearly zero temperature gradient. The NIR sensing unit, with an electrode spacing of 0.1 mm, exhibits a sensitivity approximately 70 times higher than that of symmetric electrodes. Moreover, the NIR sensing unit can be disassembled and reused, and the Au@ITO electrodes exhibit at least 5 times of reusability and stability. This mechanism allows us to construct a sensing array for spatial NIR mapping and a biomimetic system that replicates the complete “perception‑to‑orientation” behavior sequence. This work provides a material-agnostic strategy for application in ultrathin, environmentally friendly, and self-powered NIR sensing systems.

summary.how: Au nanoparticle LSPR heating, asymmetric ion adsorption/desorption at the electrode–electrolyte interface, 0.1 mm spacing, array demonstrations.
summary.impact: Low relevance. Experimental sensor device with no connection to phonon transport or the listed projects.
summary.what: Builds a rattlesnake-inspired NIR sensor using photothermal conversion at Au@ITO–graphite asymmetric electrodes with an ionogel. It produces an open-circuit voltage at near-zero temperature gradient, with about 70 times the sensitivity of symmetric electrodes.
summary.why: Conventional NIR sensing materials are limited by conversion efficiency, cooling volume and recyclability.

title: Rattlesnake-Inspired Near-Infrared Sensing Based on Photothermal-Induced Asymmetric Interfacial Ion Rearrangement

abstract: Metal–organic framework databases have grown rapidly through experimental deposition and large-scale literature extraction, yet recent analyses indicate that nearly half of their entries contain substantial structural errors. These errors propagate through high-throughput screening and machine-learning workflows, limiting the reliability of data-driven materials discovery. Repairing them is difficult because the necessary evidence is scattered across crystallographic files, synthesis descriptions, and the primary literature. Here we present LitMOF, a multi-agent framework driven by large language models that reads the original publication for each structure and cross-validates it against the deposited entry to repair errors. Applying LitMOF to the metal–organic framework subset of the Cambridge Structural Database, we assembled LitMOF-DB, a curated set of 189,567 computation-ready structures that includes 9,277 repaired entries, or 69.1% of the not-computation-ready structures in the latest CoRE MOF database. The system also recovered 8,771 synthesized but undeposited frameworks missing from existing resources. Using direct air capture screening as a case study, we show that structural errors distort predicted adsorption energies and CO 2 /H 2 O selectivity, which misranks materials, produces false positives, and omits high-performing candidates. This work offers a route toward self-correcting scientific databases and toward database curation driven by large language models.

summary.how: Multi-agent LLM pipeline applied to the CSD MOF subset. A direct air capture screening case study shows how errors distort adsorption energies and selectivity.
summary.impact: Not about thermal transport, but a concrete example of LLM agents curating atomistic data, which is relevant to automated workflows and to training-data quality for MLIPs (e.g. the AlGaN pipeline).
summary.what: LitMOF is an LLM multi-agent framework that reads the original publication for each MOF structure and cross-validates it against the deposited entry. It produced LitMOF-DB with 189,567 computation-ready structures, including 9,277 repaired entries, and recovered 8,771 synthesized but undeposited frameworks.
summary.why: Nearly half of MOF database entries contain structural errors that propagate into screening and ML workflows.

title: LitMOF: An LLM Multi-Agent for Literature-Validated Metal-Organic Frameworks Database Correction and Expansion

abstract: We present a systematic benchmark of MACE interatomic potentials for iron–nickel alloys, focusing on structural, elastic, and finite-temperature properties of chemically disordered body-centered-cubic (bcc) and face-centered-cubic (fcc) phases. The reference dataset comprises spin-polarized Perdew–Burke–Ernzerhof density-functional-theory calculations for special quasirandom structures (SQS) spanning composition, volume, and shear deformation. A system-specific MACE–sqs model trained on this dataset achieves validation errors of 2.0 meV atom − 1 for energies and 24.3 meV Å − 1 for forces. We compare MACE–sqs with several MACE foundation models, including models trained using Hubbard corrections, through equations of state, equilibrium volumes, cubic elastic properties, and thermal lattice expansion. MACE–sqs gives the most consistent overall performance for several zero-temperature structural and elastic benchmarks, although its relative performance depends on property and composition and it does not reproduce all experimental elastic trends. In the finite-temperature comparison, no single model is uniformly superior, and MACE–matpes agrees more closely with experiment for some compositions and comparison metrics. Finite-temperature calculations yield reasonable thermal-expansion coefficients near 300 K, while deviations at elevated temperatures and for magnetovolume sensitive compositions highlight the limitation of representing magnetic effects only implicitly through the spin-polarized reference data. These results define the tested application domain in which targeted SQS-based training improves upon broad foundation models and identify explicit magnetic degrees of freedom and broader configurational sampling as priorities for future development.

summary.how: Spin-polarized DFT on SQS spanning composition, volume and shear. Models are compared on equations of state, cubic elastic constants and thermal expansion.
summary.impact: Directly relevant to the InGaAs alloy project (self-trained Deep Potential vs MACE across compositions) and to MLIP failure-mode analysis. The finding that no model is uniformly best, and that magnetism is only implicit, is a useful template for comparing MLIPs on alloy κ in the Phonon Olympics.
summary.what: Systematic benchmark of MACE potentials for chemically disordered bcc/fcc Fe–Ni alloys. A system-specific MACE–sqs model, trained on spin-polarized PBE data for special quasirandom structures, reaches validation errors of 2.0 meV/atom (energy) and 24.3 meV/Å (forces). It is compared with several MACE foundation models.
summary.why: To define where targeted training beats broad foundation models for alloys with magnetic effects.

title: Capabilities and limitations of MACE interatomic potentials for Fe–Ni alloys: a systematic benchmark
venue: Modelling and Simulation in Materials Science and Engineering

abstract: Ordered crystals generally exhibit crystalline heat transport, even when a boson peak is present. Here we show that the quasi-one-dimensional single crystal ( N b 4 S e 15 I 2 ) I 2 exhibits ultralow, glass-like thermal transport: its thermal conductivity increases monotonically and reaches only 0.21 W m − 1 K − 1 at 20 K. Heat-capacity and low-frequency Raman measurements reveal a boson-peak-like excess of low-energy vibrational states. The crystal consists of a rigid phonon-carrying backbone and weakly coordinated interchain I − ions. \blue{Ab initio molecular dynamics (AIMD) reveals unusually large, strongly anisotropic, and anharmonic motion of these ions, while phonon calculations show an avoided crossing between low-frequency optical and acoustic branches, establishing acoustic–optical hybridization. Structural and AIMD evidence supports substantial involvement of the interchain subsystem in the soft low-frequency modes. A minimal theory shows how hybridization with strongly anharmonic interchain dynamics can reduce the group velocity and lifetime of acoustic-like heat carriers. These results link the boson-peak-like excess and glass-like heat transport as related but distinct consequences of coupling between a rigid heat-carrying backbone and weakly coordinated interchain degrees of freedom, suggesting a structural route to anomalous heat transport in ordered low-dimensional crystals.

summary.how: Thermal conductivity, heat-capacity and low-frequency Raman measurements, combined with AIMD, phonon calculations and a minimal theory of hybridization with anharmonic interchain modes.
summary.impact: Relevant to lattice-dynamics and anharmonicity methods in the BTE projects (e.g. BaTiO3 and SrTiO3 defect phonons). It is a mechanism case where the standard phonon-gas BTE picture may fail, so it is useful for thinking about the limits of BTE.
summary.what: Reports glass-like, ultralow thermal conductivity (0.21 W/mK at 20 K) in the ordered quasi-1D crystal (Nb4Se15I2)I2. Heat capacity and Raman show a boson-peak-like excess of low-energy states. AIMD shows strongly anharmonic, anisotropic motion of interchain I- ions, and phonon calculations show acoustic–optical avoided crossing.
summary.why: To understand how an ordered crystal can show glassy heat transport and how boson-peak-like excess relates to it.

title: Glassy heat transport from interchain rattling in an ordered quasi-one-dimensional crystal

abstract: Heterogeneous catalysts under reaction conditions have crowded surfaces where lateral interactions dictate reaction energetics. Understanding and predicting these interactions, however, remains a formidable challenge. First-principles calculations suffer from vast combinatorial complexity on crowded surfaces, while machine learning methods require large training data sets and have limited physical interpretability. We reveal a physics-based linear correlation mapping complex coverage-dependent adsorption energies directly to computationally inexpensive gas-phase pairwise interactions that are evaluated via Mie potentials. This correlation is governed by bond order conservation: as surface−adsorbate interactions weaken under crowding, adsorbate−adsorbate interactions strengthen. This correlation generalizes across metal surfaces having diverse crystal facets, surface tensions, and single- and multicomponent adsorption classes (e.g., dissociative S*, N* + O*, and nondissociative CO*). This correlation predicts coverage-dependent reaction thermodynamics for NO* dissociation and for atomic-adsorbate diffusion. Coverage-dependent trends in adsorption energies of CO*/Pt(111) agree with experimental calorimetry. Ultimately, these gas-phase pairwise interactions are a descriptor for lateral interactions of atomic and structurally simple adsorbates on structurally stable metal surfaces. The generalizability and physical interpretability of this descriptor open new avenues for modeling adsorption and reaction energies on crowded metal surfaces.
authors: Danish Uzair Bin Abdul Hamid Khan Surattee

summary.how: First-principles adsorption energies correlated against Mie-potential gas-phase interactions.
summary.impact: Low relevance. Catalysis-specific; only a general example of a physically interpretable descriptor in place of a data-hungry ML model.
summary.what: Shows a physics-based linear correlation mapping coverage-dependent adsorption energies on metal surfaces to gas-phase pairwise (Mie potential) interactions, explained by bond-order conservation. It generalizes across facets and adsorbate classes and agrees with CO/Pt(111) calorimetry.
summary.why: Lateral interactions on crowded catalyst surfaces are hard to compute and ML methods need large data sets and lack interpretability.

title: Coverage Effects in Heterogeneous Catalysis: From Fundamental Understanding to Predictive Modeling
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

abstract: Developing stable and environmentally lead-free perovskites is essential for future optoelectronic technologies. In this work, we systematically investigate the structural, mechanical, electronic, optical, thermodynamic and dynamical properties of Cs 2 CdMCl 6 (M = Mg, Si, Ge, Sn) double halide perovskites through first-principles density functional theory calculations. Both GGA-PBE and GGA-PBEsol calculations confirm the cubic Fm- 3 ¯ m crystal structure to be stable and the lattice parameters and M-Cl bond lengths are found to increase with the atomic size of M-site. The calculated Goldschmidt and octahedral tolerance factors are in good agreement with the structural possibility of the studied compounds, although Cs 2 CdSiCl 6 falls outside the preferred octahedral and Bartel criteria. All the compositions reveal ductile nature according to their Pugh’s ratio and Poisson’s ratio. The formation energy was found to be negative for all compounds. Moreover, all the compositions satisfy the Born-Huang mechanical stability criteria. The HSE06 calculations show large bandgaps, ranging from 2.13 to 4.27 eV. All compounds exhibit indirect bandgap except Cs 2 CdMgCl 6 . For all compounds, the electron effective masses ( m e * / m 0 ) are significantly lower than the hole effective masses ( m h * / m 0 ) under both the GGA-PBE and GGA-PBE + SOC approximations. Phonon dispersion calculations reveal the dynamical stability except Cs 2 CdSnCl 6 . However, ab initio molecular dynamics simulations at 300 K for 5 ps do not show significant structural distortion, implying good thermal integrity under the simulated conditions. abstract: The relative contributions of electrons and phonons to heat transport in uranium nitride (UN) and uranium dioxide (UO₂) remain incompletely resolved. DFT + U calculations are combined with three-phonon Boltzmann transport for the lattice thermal conductivity (κ L ) and with electron–phonon-limited carrier transport, in which the carrier lifetimes are obtained from the imaginary part of the electron–phonon self-energy within the self-energy relaxation-time approximation (SERTA) and compared with the constant relaxation-time approximation (CRTA). Among non-magnetic, ferromagnetic and collinear antiferromagnetic (AFM) configurations, the AFM solution is the lowest in energy for both compounds and reproduces their distinct electronic structures: a metal with a narrow magnetic pseudogap at the Fermi level in UN and a 2.29 eV Mott–Hubbard gap in UO₂. UO₂ is lattice-dominated, with κ L decreasing from 7.7 to 2.4 W m ‐1 K ‐1 between 300 and 1000 K, whereas UN is electron-dominated, with an electronic thermal conductivity increasing from 12.9 to 31.6 W m ‐1 K ‐1 over 300–1500 K. Within this electron–phonon-limited model, AFM-SERTA reproduces the measured temperature dependence of the electrical conductivity of UN, whereas the CRTA does not. Without fitting to thermal-conductivity data, this work captures the order-of-magnitude thermal-conductivity advantage of UN over UO₂, providing a first-principles route for screening advanced nuclear fuels.

summary.how: DFT+U with magnetic configurations (NM, FM, AFM), three-phonon BTE, and electron–phonon self-energy relaxation-time approximation. No fit to thermal-conductivity data.
summary.impact: Methodologically close to the phonon BTE workflow (phono3py/ALAMODE-type) and shows the value of SERTA over CRTA when electrons matter. It is not directly tied to a current project; it is only loosely transferable to the metallic/doped cases.
summary.what: First-principles study of UN and UO2 combining DFT+U, three-phonon BTE for lattice κ and electron–phonon-limited transport (SERTA vs CRTA). UO2 is lattice-dominated, with κL falling from 7.7 to 2.4 W/mK over 300–1000 K. UN is electron-dominated, with electronic κ rising from 12.9 to 31.6 W/mK over 300–1500 K.
summary.why: The relative electron and phonon contributions to heat transport in these nuclear fuels are unresolved.

title: Effects of magnetic configuration and electron–phonon scattering on thermal transport in uranium nitride and uranium dioxide

abstract: Insulating materials featuring high thermal conductivity can enhance heat removal near the electron channel in modern transistors. Ultrawide bandgap beryllium oxide (BeO) is promising owing to its high bulk thermal conductivity, but its thermal transport in ultrathin films remains largely unexplored. This study investigates phonon thermal transport in ultrathin (<30 nm) single‐crystalline (sc‐) and nanocrystalline (nc‐) BeO films grown by plasma‐enhanced atomic layer deposition (PEALD) at 150°C on GaN‐on‐Al 2 O 3 and Si substrates, respectively. The challenge of extracting cross‐plane thermal conductivity in such ultrathin films is addressed by combining frequency‐domain thermoreflectance (FDTR) with a diffusive series thermal resistor model and Monte Carlo uncertainty analysis, yielding approximately 20 and 12 W m −1 K −1 for sc‐BeO and nc‐BeO, respectively. The value obtained for sc‐BeO exceeds those reported for most dielectric thin films of comparable thickness. The FDTR‐extracted total thermal resistance data for sc‐BeO are also consistent with a ballistic transport model. Device thermal modeling indicates that employing sc‐BeO as a top‐side heat spreader reduces device thermal resistance, with greater cooling benefits at larger film thicknesses and in devices based on low‐thermal‐conductivity materials. These findings highlight the potential of PEALD BeO as a low‐thermal‐budget dielectric heat spreader for next‐generation power and radiofrequency devices.

summary.how: FDTR measurement, diffusive series resistor model, Monte Carlo uncertainty analysis, and device thermal modeling. Total resistance data are consistent with a ballistic transport model.
summary.impact: Related to the GaN/AlGaN HEMT multiscale thermal modeling project: the device modeling of a BeO heat spreader on GaN and the ballistic-transport consistency give data for validation. The work is mainly experimental, so relevance is moderate.
summary.what: Measures cross-plane thermal conductivity of ultrathin (<30 nm) PEALD BeO films on GaN-on-Al2O3 and Si using FDTR, a series-resistor model and Monte Carlo uncertainty analysis. Values are about 20 W/mK (single-crystalline) and 12 W/mK (nanocrystalline). Device thermal modeling shows sc-BeO as a top-side heat spreader reduces device thermal resistance.
summary.why: High-κ insulators near the channel could improve heat removal in transistors, but ultrathin BeO transport was unexplored.

title: High Thermal Conductivity in Ultrathin Single‐Crystalline BeO Films

abstract: Composite materials provide a versatile platform for suppressing lattice thermal conductivity through secondary phases and engineered interfaces that effectively scatter phonons while minimizing deterioration of electronic transport, offering a promising route toward high‐performance thermoelectrics. Herein, we systematically review how composite architectures manipulate thermal transport and enhance the thermoelectric figure of merit. We begin with classical phonon theory to understand the thermal transport in single phase. By establishing performance benchmarks for pristine matrix, we then compare various reported composite thermoelectric materials across low‐, mid‐, and high‐temperature regimes. The experimental trends are rationalized by the mean‐field theory, interfacial mechanisms (acoustic mismatch model and diffuse mismatch model), and nanostructure‐induced size effects. Next, we examine different compositing strategies to modulate the phononic contribution to thermal conductivity, including porous structure, nanoprecipitates, magnetic phases, crystalline–amorphous hybrid, and superlattice. Extending from materials to thermoelectric devices, we discuss the critical challenges associated with incorporating composite thermoelectric materials into thermoelectric devices, with particular emphasis on non‐uniform heat field, and thermal expansion mismatch for device reliability and operational stability. Finally, we outline practical design principles, highlighting opportunities for reproducible materials fabrication, interface engineering, and synergistic optimization of phonon and carrier transport to accelerate the development of next‐generation composite thermoelectrics.

summary.how: Literature review with benchmarks across temperature regimes and design principles.
summary.impact: Background on AMM/DMM and interface scattering relevant to the interfacial transport work (GaN/Al2O3, BAs interfaces). Mostly experimental and thermoelectric-focused, so moderate relevance as a reference.
summary.what: Review of how composite architectures (porous structures, nanoprecipitates, magnetic phases, crystalline–amorphous hybrids, superlattices) suppress lattice thermal conductivity in thermoelectrics. It covers phonon theory, AMM/DMM interface models, mean-field theory and device-level issues such as non-uniform heat fields and thermal expansion mismatch.
summary.why: To suppress lattice κ with secondary phases and interfaces without degrading electronic transport.

title: Thermal Transport in Composite Thermoelectrics: From Phonon Scattering Mechanisms to Device Reliability

abstract: Heteroepitaxial growth of high-quality β-Ga2O3 remains fundamentally challenged by large lattice and thermal mismatches with conventional foreign substrates, which inevitably induce high threading dislocation densities and severe residual strain, ultimately limiting the performance and reliability of solar-blind photodetectors. In this work, we propose and demonstrate a quasi-van der Waals epitaxial strategy using artificially synthesized fluorophlogopite (F-mica) as a thermally robust, atomically smooth template for metal-organic chemical vapor deposition growth of β-Ga2O3. By combining x-ray photoelectron spectroscopy and first-principles calculations, we reveal a unique interfacial mechanism where localized strong chemical bonds (Ga–O–Si bonding) coexist with weak van der Waals forces, which simultaneously defines the epitaxial orientation and enables efficient strain relaxation. This hybrid growth mode yields a high-purity, preferentially (-201)-oriented β-Ga2O3 film with an ultralow in-plane lattice strain of 0.3% and ∼30% reduction in total dislocation density compared to sapphire-based counterparts. Leveraging this high-crystalline-quality film, we fabricate metal–semiconductor–metal solar-blind photodetectors that achieve a remarkable detectivity of 1.8 × 1012 Jones and an ultraviolet/visible rejection ratio of 104, representing approximately 21-fold improvement over devices on sapphire. This study not only elucidates the quasi-van der Waals epitaxial mechanism but also provides a viable route toward high-performance flexible optoelectronics.

summary.how: MOCVD growth, XPS and first-principles calculations of the interface (Ga–O–Si bonds plus van der Waals). The film shows 0.3% in-plane strain and ~30% lower dislocation density than on sapphire; detectivity is 1.8×10^12 Jones.
summary.impact: Low relevance: mostly experimental growth and device work on Ga2O3 photodetectors, with no thermal transport content for the GaN/Al2O3 interface or dislocation projects.
summary.what: Quasi-van der Waals epitaxy of β-Ga2O3 on fluorophlogopite mica, with solar-blind photodetectors fabricated on the films.
summary.why: Large lattice and thermal mismatch on conventional substrates causes high threading dislocation density and residual strain.

title: Quasi-van der Waals epitaxy of low-strain β -Ga2O3 on fluorophlogopite enables high-performance solar-blind photodetectors

abstract: At cryogenic temperatures, phonons become one of the dominant energy carriers and thus can strongly influence the performance of electronic and sensing devices. Phonon transport departs fundamentally from the diffusive behavior typically seen at higher temperatures, as cryogenic phonons exhibit ballistic transport, propagate as waves, and possess large coherence lengths. Since phonons at milliKelvin temperatures do not follow Fourier's law and are only weakly coupled to electrons, controlling and isolating phonon propagation becomes a significant challenge. Conventional approaches to thermal isolation rely on diffusion-based boundary scattering or amorphous materials, offering limited control over the spectral properties of transported phonons. In this work, we present a wave-mechanics-based framework that predicts phonon transmission and thermal resistance of arbitrarily thick superlattices while retaining all acoustic branches, mode-conversion pathways, and angles of incidence. By enforcing phase coherence, our model predicts frequency-dependent transmission through arbitrary multi-layered structures. We use a genetic algorithm (NSGA-II) to efficiently select both materials and layer thicknesses. Our success criterion is that constituent layers satisfy the quarter-wavelength condition of the dominant phonon frequencies at a target temperature. This strategy identifies novel bilayer combinations that achieve thermal resistance of up to 3000 times greater than previously reported superlattices. The identified superlattices are poised to advance any technology that relies on coherent acoustic scattering, from ultra-low-temperature thermal insulation in superconducting flip-chip assemblies to phonon-blocking components in micro- and nano-electromechanical systems. summary.impact: Moderately relevant: coherent interface and multilayer phonon transmission is related to the GaN/Al2O3 interface and SrTiO3 grain boundary work, and the optimisation approach could inspire band-discretization checks in JAX-BTE. The cryogenic regime is far from the GaN HEMT operating range.

title: Coherent phonon blocking in superlattices

abstract: Reducing the thermal conductivity of ceramic coatings requires control of heattransport across multiple length scales without sacrificing adhesion, fracture resistance, oxidation resistance, or thermal-cycle life. In many electrically insulatingceramic coatings, lattice vibrations (phonons) dominate heat conduction. Their transport can be impeded by mass and strain-field disorder, oxygen vacancies, grain boundaries, pores, phase interfaces, and nanoscale inclusions. This study proposes a multiscale materials-design framework for ceramic coatings based on rare-earth zirconates and high-entropy oxides, with carefully controlled defect populations and hierarchical microstructures.The theoretical basis combines the phonon Boltzmann transport equation (BTE),mode-dependent scattering lifetimes, Matthiessen-type rate addition as a first approximation, point-defect scattering, and effective-medium descriptions of coatinglayers. The framework emphasizes that lowering intrinsic lattice conductivity alonedoes not guarantee a better coating: radiation, gas-filled porosity, interfacial resistance, sintering, and mechanical damage can change both measured effective conductivity and service performance. Candidate systems—including high-entropy rare-earth zirconates, rare-earth niobates, disordered fluorite oxides, and multilayer zirconate/zirconia architectures— are treated as research directions rather than universally optimal materials.A staged workflow is proposed, linking computational screening, synthesis, coatingdeposition, thermal-property measurements, microscopy, and thermal cycling. abstract: Altermagnetic (AM) two-dimensional materials provide a promising platform for exploring the interplay between unconventional magnetism and heat transport, yet their anharmonic phonon dynamics remain largely unexplored. Here, we systematically investigate the lattice thermal transport of AM MnX2 (X = S, Se) monolayers with pentagonal structures using first-principles calculations and phonon Boltzmann transport theory considering both three-phonon (3ph) and four-phonon (4ph) scattering. We establish that both systems favor the antiferromagnetic (AFM) ground state and exhibit AM band splitting, and the harmonic phonon dispersions are only weakly affected by the ferromagnetic (FM) magnetic ordering. Bonding analysis further reveals that the chalcogen–chalcogen dimer interactions play a crucial role in the distinct lattice dynamics of MnS2 and MnSe2. We then find that both systems exhibit low lattice thermal conductivities κL, which are substantially reduced by 66.2% and 87.7% upon inclusion of 4ph scattering at 300 K. The pronounced anharmonicity is evidenced by large negative Grüneisen parameters up to −50 of the acoustic modes and strong low-frequency phonon scattering by 4ph processes. Analysis of mean free path (MFP) and channel-resolved 3ph scattering rates attribute the lower κL of MnSe2 to its lower phonon group velocities and stronger acoustic–optical scattering. These results establish higher-order anharmonicity as an important factor in the thermal transport of pentagonal altermagnets and highlight their potential for thermal management and spin-caloritronic applications.

summary.how: First-principles calculations with phonon BTE including 3ph and 4ph scattering; bonding analysis, Grüneisen parameters, MFP and channel-resolved scattering rates. Four-phonon scattering lowers κL by 66.2% (MnS2) and 87.7% (MnSe2) at 300 K, with Grüneisen parameters down to −50 for acoustic modes.

abstract: The structural and adsorption properties of hydrogen-passivated armchair stanene nanoribbons (ASnNRs) decorated with Ti, Mn, and Ni were investigated using density functional theory (DFT). The calculations were complemented by Boltzmann transport theory and Crystal Graph Convolutional Neural Network (CGCNN) predictions. Among the investigated transition-metal configurations, the hollow site was energetically preferred, and Mn-decorated ASnNR was selected as a representative system for detailed gas-sensing analysis. The adsorption strength on Mn-ASnNR follows the order SO2 > NO2 > NH3, indicating stronger interactions with SO2 and NO2. Gas adsorption substantially modifies the electronic, magnetic, optical, thermoelectric, and charge-transport properties of Mn-ASnNR, while CGCNN predictions indicate relatively minor variations in its thermomechanical parameters. These results highlight the potential of Mn-decorated ASnNR for toxic-gas sensing and related optoelectronic applications.

abstract: The present study analyzes the electronic structure, optical, mechanical, and thermoelectric characteristics of La 2 XS 4 (X = Cd, Mg) chalcogenides using the DFT approach, demonstrating clear structure–property correlations. Both compounds are thermodynamically stable, with negative formation energies (−2.12 and −2.27 eV/atom) and strong cohesive energies (−3.07 and −3.26 eV/atom). La 2 MgS 4 is more stable and has stronger bonding due to its ionic Mg‐S contacts and tight lattice. The two materials are stable and ductile with (B/G > 1.75). La 2 CdS 4 is stiffer with B = 40.89 GPa and Y = 56.25 GPa, but La 2 MgS 4 has better ductility, isotropy, and metallic bonding. Both materials have high dielectric constants (∼6.5–6.7), substantial UV absorption (4–6 eV). La 2 CdS 4 has higher polarizability, resulting in increased optical intensity and refractive response. Both La 2 MgS 4 and La 2 CdS 4 demonstrate positive Seebeck coefficients and intrinsic semiconducting behavior. La 2 MgS 4 has greater thermopower, lower κ e , and improved ZT due to sharper band edges. Overall, Mg substitution improves stability and thermoelectric efficiency, but Cd substitution improves optical strength and electrical transmission.

abstract: This work presents a comprehensive electrothermal analysis of power loss and junction temperature in a 400V/200V, 3 KW DC-DC buck converter operating at switching frequencies from 50 to 200 kHz for electrical vehicle (EV) charging applications. The performance of a GaN systems GS66508B gallium nitride (GaN) is evaluated and compared with a silicon (Si) STMicroelectronics STP11NM80 MOSFET and a silicon carbide (SiC) Wolfspeed C3M0120065D MOSFET under identical converter topology, passive component values and operating conditions. The converter employs an inductance of 270μH and an output capacitance of 100μF. Semiconductor power losses are evaluated using LT spice considering conduction and switching loss components. The conduction loss is calculated from the RMS drain current and on-state resistance, while turn-on and turn-off switching energies are obtained directly by integrating the simulated vDS.iD waveforms, thereby avoiding idealised linear switching transition assumptions. At the baseline operating point of 400 V input, 100 kHz switching frequency and 3 kW rated load, the calculated semiconductor losses are 7.5126 W, 19.6845 W and 47.8417 W for GaN, SiC and Si, respectively, with corresponding simulated converter efficiencies of 99.75%, 99.34% and 98.39%. The calculated semiconductor losses are applied as a dynamic heat source to Cauer RC thermal network comprising junction-to-case, case-to-heatsink and heatsink-to-ambient elements to accurately estimate the transient junction temperature (Tj) under varying switching frequencies. The GaN device shows the lowest semiconductor power loss and junction temperature under specified operating conditions, indicating its potential for high frequency EV charging applications.

abstract: First-principles calculations combined with Boltzmann transport theory were used to investigate the electronic and phonon transport properties of monolayer R-graphyne and Ab-stacked bilayer R-graphyne. HSE06 calculations indicate metallic electronic structures for both systems. The bilayer exhibits shorter phonon lifetimes and lower lattice thermal conductivity than the monolayer. At 300 K, the calculated lattice thermal conductivities are 150.97 and 50.60 W m−1 K−1 for the monolayer and bilayer, respectively. The maximum calculated n-type power factors are 0.36 and 0.944 W m−1 K−2, respectively, both at 300 K. Within the adopted deformation-potential and relaxation-time approximations, the overall maximum n-type ZT values are 0.889 for the monolayer at 700 K and 1.943 for the bilayer at 300 K. However, the relative advantage of the bilayer depends on temperature: its maximum n-type ZT exceeds that of the monolayer at 300 and 500 K but is lower at 700 K. These results illustrate how Ab stacking modifies the balance between electronic and phonon transport. The predicted thermoelectric performance remains model dependent, and the carrier densities associated with the optimal values have not been experimentally established for R-graphyne.

summary.impact: Low relevance: a standard DFT+BTE workflow on a 2D carbon material with no direct link to the GaN, InGaAs or BAs projects.
summary.what: First-principles plus Boltzmann transport study of monolayer and Ab-stacked bilayer R-graphyne. Lattice κ at 300 K is 150.97 (monolayer) and 50.60 W/m/K (bilayer); max n-type ZT is 0.889 (monolayer, 700 K) and 1.943 (bilayer, 300 K).

abstract: Cobalt-based half-Heusler (HH) thermoelectric compounds with a valence 18-electron (18-e) count are known for their favorable electrical transport properties and thermal stability. However, their inherently high lattice thermal conductivities present a significant challenge for thermoelectric performance. Here, we explore the potential of double half-Heusler compounds, X 2 FeNiZ 2 (X = Ti, Zr, Hf; Z = Sb, Bi), formed by substituting Co with Fe and Ni, following the 18-valence electron count rule. These compounds exhibit a reduction in lattice thermal conductivity. This amounts to approximately 20% ∼ 40% reductions as compared to the ternary HH counterparts. This decrease is due to the chemical nature of the compounds, specifically a combination of strong and weak chemical bonds. The resulting heterogeneous bonding environment enhances anharmonicity and phonon scattering. Furthermore, the electronic band structures show features that are favorable for thermoelectric performance, including carrier pocket degeneracy, band warping and anisotropic carrier pockets. Thus, electron count preserving site splitting to form the double half-Heusler structure, is an effective strategy for reducing the lattice thermal conductivity, while maintaining favorable electronic characteristics.

summary.how: First-principles calculations of lattice thermal conductivity and band structure; the reduction is attributed to heterogeneous strong/weak bonding that enhances anharmonicity and phonon scattering.
summary.impact: Low-moderate relevance. It is a phonon and anharmonicity analysis in a material outside the reader's projects, but the bonding-heterogeneity argument is a useful reference for interpreting κ in alloys such as InGaAs.
summary.what: Computational study of double half-Heusler compounds X2FeNiZ2 (X = Ti, Zr, Hf; Z = Sb, Bi) following the 18-electron rule, with 20-40% lower lattice thermal conductivity than ternary half-Heuslers.
summary.why: Cobalt-based 18-electron half-Heuslers have good electronic properties but high lattice thermal conductivity.

title: Bonding heterogeneity induced ultralow lattice thermal conductivity in double half-Heusler compounds X 2 FeNi Z 2 ( X = Ti , Zr , Hf ; Z = Sb , Bi )

abstract: Replacing lead in halide perovskites without sacrificing their optoelectronic versatility remains a central challenge in sustainable materials chemistry. Bismuth(III), isoelectronic with Pb2+, offers a chemically robust route to this goal, but its compounds are typically evaluated for a single function, namely light absorption, photocatalysis, or thermal transport in isolation. In this work, we show that a single, mechanochemically synthesized layered halide platform, Cs3Bi2Br9 and its iodine-substituted analogue Cs3Bi2Br6I3, integrates all three. High-resolution synchrotron diffraction resolves the corner-sharing [Bi(Br,I)6] octahedral layers and reveals a stereochemically active Bi3+ lone pair whose signature, being pronounced, temperature-dependent atomic displacement anisotropy; we quantify with a site-resolved Debye model. This lone-pair-driven lattice softness rationalizes an intrinsically low thermal conductivity (~0.15–0.25 W m−1K−1), further suppressed by iodine substitution. Group-theory-assigned Raman and infrared phonons, validated against DFT lattice dynamics, and direct optical gaps of 2.65 and 2.20 eV place both compounds’ absorption edges in the visible range. We demonstrate that Cs3Bi2Br9 photocatalytically degrades the organic dye Rhodamine B roughly 75-fold faster than direct photolysis and retains full activity over four reuse cycles. These results establish compositional Br/I tuning as a single structural handle for co-engineering optical, thermal and catalytic function in lead-free layered halides.

summary.how: Synchrotron diffraction with a site-resolved Debye model, Raman/IR with group theory, DFT lattice dynamics, and photocatalysis tests on Rhodamine B.
summary.impact: Low relevance. It is mostly experimental and none of the projects uses this material. Only the DFT lattice-dynamics validation of the measured phonons is loosely transferable.
summary.what: Experimental study of mechanochemically synthesized Cs3Bi2Br9 and Cs3Bi2Br6I3: synchrotron diffraction, Raman/IR phonons checked against DFT lattice dynamics, low thermal conductivity (about 0.15-0.25 W/m/K), optical gaps, and photocatalytic dye degradation.
summary.why: Seeks lead-free halide perovskite alternatives that combine optical, thermal and catalytic function.

title: A multifunctional lead-free layered halide: lone-pair-driven phonon softening, tunable optical gaps, and photocatalytic dye degradation in Cs3Bi2Br9−xIx

abstract: The adsorption of technologically relevant gas molecules (NH 3 , CO 2 , H 2 , H 2 O, O 2 , NO 2 , CO, and SO 2 ) on a Na-decorated GaP/silicene heterostructure is systematically investigated using first-principles calculations combined with CGCNN predictions. All molecules exhibit negative adsorption energies, with NO 2 , SO 2 , and NH 3 showing the strongest binding. NO 2 and SO 2 induce spin polarization and finite magnetic moments, governed by charge transfer and orbital hybridization. Gas adsorption significantly modulates optical and thermoelectric responses, particularly in the low-energy region. CGCNN results reveal a reduction in mechanical stiffness ( B, G ), most pronounced for NO 2 , alongside a slight increase in Debye temperature, while the thermal expansion coefficient remains nearly unchanged (∼6.0 × 10 −5 K −1 ), indicating preserved lattice anharmonicity. These findings highlight the potential of this heterostructure for selective gas sensing and thermoelectric applications.

abstract: Driven by the demand for high-performance power electronics, GaN, a wide-bandgap semiconductor, suffers from degraded epitaxial quality due to interfacial defects. AlN is widely used as GaN epitaxial template, where twin defects modify local atomic stacking and crystal orientation. This work performs large-scale molecular dynamics simulations at 1700–2500 K to comparatively investigate GaN crystallization on a constructed twinned AlN/GaN configuration and an untwinned cubic reference under identical conditions. Atomic diffusion, ordering-front propagation and cubic–hexagonal phase competition are quantified via structural transition matrices. Results show that increasing temperature generally promotes structural ordering within the 3 ns simulation window, with growth evolving from slow heterogeneous ordering toward rapid early ordering followed by local structural adjustment. For the twinned system, four simulations with independent initial-velocity seeds at each temperature show an overall increase in the mean fully ordered fraction after 3 ns, from 13.44% at 1700 K to 68.34% at 2500 K, with appreciable variability at intermediate temperatures. Transient atomic mobility depends on the observation window and should be distinguished from accumulated structural ordering. In the trajectories compared, the untwinned template favors conditional entry into Cubic-family environments across the investigated temperature range, while the twinned configuration shows this tendency from 1900 to 2500 K. The untwinned reference shows faster disorder elimination and greater cubic retention, while the constructed twinned configuration shows more interfamily reconstruction at most temperatures. abstract: Machine learning (ML) has emerged as a powerful approach for accelerating the discovery of thermoelectric (TE) materials, yet many models suffer from limited generalizability. Here we present a robust ML framework for predicting the thermoelectric figure of merit (zT) in half-Heusler (hH) compounds, emphasizing prediction of previously unseen compositions. A principal component analysis (PCA)-based train/test splitting strategy is introduced to generate representative partitions of chemical space. Bayesian hyperparameter optimization is combined with correlation-based k-best feature selection for Random Forest, XGBoost, and Neural Network models, together with the interpretable SISSO symbolic-regression method. Relative to the full set of 118 input features, the optimized feature subsets reduce the test RMSE by 16-27%. SHAP and SISSO analyses identify temperature, A-site dopant concentration, and A-site heat of vaporization as the most important descriptors of zT. The framework is validated through prediction of previously unexplored compositions, recovery of literature-reported optimal zT values for established hH systems, and first-principles calculations for the new compounds CeCoBi and CeIrBi, which exhibit favorable electronic transport properties. The framework is further applied to high-throughput screening of the doped hH chemical space, covering about 2.46 million elemental substitution combinations across 631 thermodynamically screened parent matrices under stability constraints. This screening yields a concise set of promising candidates for future study. Overall, the work establishes a generalizable workflow for reliable data-driven thermoelectric materials discovery.

summary.how: Bayesian hyperparameter optimization with correlation-based k-best feature selection (test RMSE reduced 16-27% vs. all 118 features); SHAP and SISSO for interpretation; first-principles checks on CeCoBi and CeIrBi; screening of about 2.46 million doped substitutions over 631 parent matrices.
summary.impact: Low relevance to the GaN, InGaAs and BAs projects, since it targets electronic zT rather than phonon transport. The PCA-based splitting for out-of-distribution testing and the feature-importance analysis could loosely inform MLIP data-efficiency and failure-mode studies.
summary.what: Presents an ML framework (Random Forest, XGBoost, neural network, plus SISSO symbolic regression) for predicting zT of half-Heusler compounds, using a PCA-based train/test split to test on unseen compositions.
summary.why: Many thermoelectric ML models generalize poorly to new chemistries.

abstract: Zintl-phase materials are promising thermoelectrics due to their good carrier transport and low lattice thermal conductivity (κL). Using first-principles calculations, the Boltzmann transport equation (BTE), and dual-phonon theory, we investigate the cation-driven vibrational hierarchy and thermoelectric properties of the ternary Zintl phase KCaBi. The rattling-like vibrations induced by weakly bound interlayer K atoms, coupled with the high-temperature crossover from conventional phonon propagation to diffuson-like thermal transport, endow the material with a low κL. The out-of-plane (along the c-axis) κL ranges from ≈ 0.15 W m−1 K−1 under Criterion I (Crit. I) to ≈ 0.27 W m−1 K−1 under Criterion III (Crit. III) within the dual-phonon theory at 700 K. The rigid [Ca–Bi]− framework and the multi-valley valence band enable efficient in-plane carrier transport, yielding an in-plane thermoelectric figure of merit (ZT) of ≈ 2.28 under Crit. III and ≈ 2.52 under Crit. I for p-type KCaBi at 700 K. Meanwhile, n-type KCaBi exhibits out-of-plane ZT of ≈ 1.38 (Crit. III) to ≈ 1.92 (Crit. I) at potentially more accessible doping concentrations of 1018 cm−3. We elucidate how bonding heterogeneity affects phonon and electron transport properties in Zintl-phase KCaBi, offering a heuristic approach for designing advanced hierarchical thermoelectrics.

summary.how: DFT, phonon BTE, and dual-phonon theory covering both propagating phonons and diffuson-like transport; results reported under two criteria (Crit. I and Crit. III).
summary.impact: Relevant methodologically: it combines BTE with a diffuson/crossover treatment for strongly anharmonic, rattling-like systems, which relates to the BTE and lattice-dynamics side of the BAs and InGaAs work. The material is not one of the reader's projects.
summary.what: First-principles, BTE and dual-phonon-theory study of the Zintl phase KCaBi, finding very low out-of-plane κL (about 0.15-0.27 W/m/K at 700 K) and p-type in-plane ZT of about 2.3-2.5.
summary.why: Zintl phases are promising thermoelectrics, and the link between bonding heterogeneity and low κL needs to be understood.

abstract: A profound methodological divide separates top-down macroscopic rate law identification from bottom-up, first-principles microkinetic modeling. While top-down macroscopic models often oversimplify underlying chemistry and fail to capture localized kinetic variations, bottom-up microkinetic simulations provide an exceptionally detailed look at elementary reaction pathways. However, these complex microscopic networks are frequently bottlenecked by uncertainties in both their kinetic parameters and topologies and remain too computationally demanding for full-scale reactor engineering. To bridge this gap, we present a methodology that leverages first-principles simulations for automated library generation, circumventing the bottleneck of scarce experimental data. Central to this pipeline is the novel Linearized Ensemble Motif Operator Network framework, which extracts the underlying effective kinetic information by filtering key kinetic motifs from symbolic expressions, effectively distilling intricate microkinetic networks down to simple, chemically interpretable macroscopic rate laws. This pre-compiled motif library is integrated into a sparse model identification architecture with derivative ensembles (SMIDE). To robustly handle experimental noise, SMIDE generates an ensemble of splines from heteroscedastic noise realizations to capture derivative uncertainty. Through multi-objective optimization, the framework maps out a comprehensive Pareto front of candidate models. This approach transforms rate law discovery from a simple curve-fitting exercise into a rigorous statistical analysis of the kinetic mechanisms supported by the physical system, eliminating the need for manually predefined structural libraries.

summary.how: Key kinetic motifs are filtered from symbolic expressions into a pre-compiled library; SMIDE uses ensembles of splines from heteroscedastic noise realizations and multi-objective optimization to produce a Pareto front of candidate models.

summary.what: A methodology that uses first-principles simulations to automatically generate libraries for identifying effective macroscopic rate laws from kinetic data, based on a Linearized Ensemble Motif Operator Network framework and a sparse identification architecture (SMIDE).
summary.why: Top-down rate law models oversimplify chemistry, while bottom-up microkinetic models are uncertain and too expensive for reactor engineering.

title: Microkinetically informed library generation for modeling effective rate laws from kinetic data

abstract: ABSTRACT As the semiconductor industry increasingly pivots toward “More than Moore” and “More Moore” paradigms, heterogeneous integration has emerged as a pivotal strategy for achieving system‐level performance breakthroughs. However, residual stress inherent to the integration of dissimilar materials represents a critical bottleneck, directly threatening the integrity and reliability of these advanced systems. Heteroepitaxy, as a representative example, is inherently constrained by stress accumulation, which limits epilayer thickness, increases threading dislocation density (TDD), and degrades device reliability. Here, we present a strain‐inversion strategy that effectively transfers misfit‐induced stress from the epilayer into the substrate stack. Through co‐designed theoretical modeling and experimental validation, we introduce 4H‐SiC/SiO 2 /polycrystalline‐ceramic‐AlN integrated substrates, and demonstrate metalorganic chemical vapor deposition (MOCVD) growth of 53‐µm‐thick, stress‐free heteroepitaxial GaN films. The films exhibit outstanding structural quality, with full‐width‐at‐half‐maximum (FWHM) values of x‐ray rocking curve of 83 and 119 arcsec for the (002) and (102) planes, respectively, and a TDD of 5 × 10 7 cm −2 . These results not only set a new thickness record for MOCVD‐grown heteroepitaxial GaN but also achieve crystal quality comparable to state‐of‐the‐art benchmarks. Our approach establishes strain‐inverted epitaxy as a highly promising platform for high‐performance nitride devices and paves the way for producing low‐cost and strain‐free GaN and AlN substrates.

abstract: Uranium dioxide (UO2) undergoes defect formation and microstructural changes under reactor irradiation, making atomic-scale modeling crucial for predicting its long-term thermomechanical performance. In this work, the paramagnetic state of bulk UO2 is simulated using non-spin-polarized density functional theory (DFT) without Hubbard-U corrections to ensure a consistent, computationally tractable reference dataset. To bypass the high cost of direct ab initio molecular dynamics (MD), we developed a Behler–Parrinello high-dimensional neural network potential (HDNNP) optimized with an active-learning framework. The training database was constructed from variable-cell MD trajectories across various temperatures and pressures, calculated using the Quantum ESPRESSO package. The resulting HDNNP achieves outstanding accuracy, yielding energy and force test RMSEs of 1.46×10-4 eV/atom and 8.73×10-3 eV/Å, respectively. Implemented in LAMMPS, the potential accurately predicts the equilibrium lattice parameter and single-crystal elastic constants (C11, C12, C44) of UO2. The predicted elastic constants exhibit excellent agreement with experimental data and DFT+U benchmarks, with relative errors remaining within 2–17%. This highlights the model’s capability to serve as a high-fidelity, computationally efficient surrogate for large-scale simulations of the mechanical behavior of nuclear fuels.

summary.how: Training data come from variable-cell MD trajectories at various temperatures and pressures computed with Quantum ESPRESSO using non-spin-polarized DFT without Hubbard-U. Reported test RMSEs are 1.46e-4 eV/atom (energy) and 8.73e-3 eV/Å (forces); elastic constants agree with experiment and DFT+U within 2-17%.

summary.what: An active-learning Behler-Parrinello high-dimensional neural network potential (HDNNP) for paramagnetic UO2, implemented in LAMMPS, with exchange-correlation functional screening.
summary.why: Atomic-scale modeling is needed to predict long-term thermomechanical performance of UO2 nuclear fuel under irradiation, while direct ab initio MD is too costly.

title: Exchange–Correlation Functional Screening and Development of a High Dimensional Neural Network Interatomic Potential for UO2

abstract: We investigate the structural, electronic, and phonon transport properties of GaSe0.5Te0.5 and InSe0.5Te0.5 systems in centrosymmetric (CS) and non-centrosymmetric (NCS) configurations using first-principles calculations combined with Boltzmann transport theory. Structural optimization and stability analysis confirm the feasibility of both configurations. Our results show that crystal symmetry plays a decisive role in governing charge and phonon transport. The centrosymmetric phases exhibit higher carrier mobility, reaching 5407 cm²/Vs for CS-GaSe0.5Te0.5 and 1872 cm²/Vs for CSInSe0.5Te0.5, due to reduced carrier–phonon scattering and more symmetric electronic band dispersion. Interestingly, while both Ga and In-based systems are expected to show superior electrical conductivity due to “conductive network” overlap, the additional antibonding character from In–Te bonds in Insystem may further suppress phonon transport, resulting in reduced lattice thermal conductivity. Additionally, inversion-symmetry breaking in the NCS structures enhances lattice anharmonicity, strengthens phonon scattering, and reduces phonon group velocities, leading to a strong suppression of in-plane lattice thermal conductivity. Moreover, the absence of inversion symmetry in the NCSconfiguration induces Rashba-type spin splitting, which modifies the electronic band structure and enhances the Seebeck coefficient. As a result of this symmetry-driven interplay between electronic and phononic transport, NCS-InSe0.5Te0.5 exhibits the best thermoelectric performance, achieving a maximum ZT of ~2.7 at 600 K. These results highlight symmetry engineering as an effective strategy to optimize thermoelectric efficiency in layered chalcogenide systems.

summary.how: Stated results: inversion-symmetry breaking enhances anharmonicity, strengthens phonon scattering and reduces group velocities, suppressing in-plane lattice thermal conductivity; the NCS-InSe0.5Te0.5 reaches a maximum ZT of about 2.7 at 600 K. Specific codes are not stated in the abstract.
summary.impact: Low relevance. A conventional DFT+BTE thermoelectric study on materials outside the owner's projects; the symmetry-anharmonicity argument is of mild interest only.
summary.what: First-principles plus Boltzmann transport study of structural, electronic and phonon transport in GaSe0.5Te0.5 and InSe0.5Te0.5 in centrosymmetric and non-centrosymmetric configurations.
summary.why: To test how crystal symmetry governs charge and phonon transport for thermoelectric design in layered chalcogenides.

title: Breaking of inversion symmetry as a design parameter for thermoelectric transport in M Se 0.5 Te 0.5 ( M = Ga , In )

abstract: Two-dimensional semiconductors, such as monolayer MoS 2 , combine a technologically useful band gap with a thickness of three atomic planes. The entire carrier density then lies within a few Å of the surface, which makes them useful as field-effect-transistor channels and as chemically sensitive devices. Device design for MoS 2 needs a transport model whose scattering rates are computed rather than calibrated, whose predictions are tested against experiment, and that spans the scales from electron-phonon coupling to terminal current and sensor response. We present a self-consistent ensemble Monte Carlo (EMC) framework for monolayer MoS 2 built on the ViennaEMC solver, which couples a Boltzmann transport model to Poisson’s equation with degenerate free-carrier statistics. The transport model carries wavevector-dependent acoustic, polar-optical, homopolar and intervalley phonon scattering within and between the K valleys and the spin–orbit-split Q valleys, together with remote substrate phonons, screened charged impurities and surface roughness. Every intrinsic input of the transport model is computed from first principles for this work, namely the band structure of the K and Q valleys, the phonon energies, sound velocities and dielectric response, and the electron-phonon couplings from density-functional perturbation theory matrix elements at 34 explicit phonon wavevectors and from Wannier interpolation with the two-dimensional long-range treatment. The model therefore contains no fitted transport parameter and no coupling taken from another calculation, and its scattering rates are checked against an independent solution of the linearised Boltzmann equation with the same couplings.
